newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss money market grows cautious, SNB offers cash.
newsitem.headline: Swiss money market grows cautious, SNB offers cash.

text.p: Swiss money market rates firmed in early trading despite a liquidity injection by the Swiss National Bank (SNB) and dealers were beginning to express their confusion about the outlook for short-term rates.

The SNB conducted 72-day dollar/Swiss currency swaps and offered one-month funds at 1-7/16 percent, a rate dealers described as relatively expensive. They said this morning's activity had them guessing about the central bank's current policy.
"We have the feeling they (the SNB) are changing policy," one dealer said.
In the recent past the SNB's has agressively sought to slow any dramatic advances of the Swiss franc in the foreign exchange market.
But the mark has dipped below 82.00 centimes recently and is currently trading below 82.50. Germany is Switzerland's main trading partner.
"The last time we were at 82.50 the SNB provided large sums of liquidity at favourable levels," one dealer said.

He said the SNB is either feeling somewhat helpless with regard to the mark's slide, or they are not too concerned given the fact that the franc is still weaker against the dollar and other currencies.
They might also be beginning to gradually tighten now that a gradual Swiss economic recovery is on track, he added.
"I don't have the feeling they are tightening, but maybe they feel helpless as to what they can do," he said.
Tomorrow/next money was quoted at 1-9/16 to 1-11/16 percent in morning trading and one month money was at 1-7/16 to 1-9/16 percent. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
